graph.name: Draft a fictional inner voice
graph.description:
Draft a short fictional inner thought as optional next-reply guidance.

Lesson: Express Inner Voice produces fictional Text with a second model call. Compose accepts that Text through a named section and makes explicitly labeled Guidance; Text and Guidance are different artifact types.

Limitations: This is authored fictional text, not private model reasoning. Host narration permissions still determine whether it appears in the reply.

Opening installs an unassigned copy. Bind local model roles and provide the documented evidence before running.

Pre: at most 2 auxiliary calls. Preview before publishing or applying.

Try changing:
Change Inner Voice's requested length from 35–55 words to one sentence and lower its Output tokens from 1024 to 512; inspect whether it adds something beyond the spoken line.
Change Compose's label and boundary to request subtext only, with no quoted thought; compare how the host uses the same fictional Text as optional direction.

Documentation specimen (does not seed chat or actor memory):

Spoken line: "Of course you can stay." The guest's arrival is unexpected.

Fictional inner voice: One night. She could manage one night without letting the old argument back into the house.

Evidence → assessment → fictional Text: Wire Scene+State to Reflect, Reflect assessment to Express Inner Voice, and the same Scene/State to Express's optional evidence pins. Analysis and Prose profiles remain local and unresolved.

Text → labeled Guidance → host: Wire Express out→Compose section.InnerVoice, then Compose→Guidance. The visible label belongs to authored template text and node aliases; Guidance itself exposes only Budget tokens.

What inner voice means: The prose is fictional characterization. Host narration permissions govern whether it appears as thought, subtext or neither. It is not private model reasoning and does not settle a new memory episode.

Invitation and old argument (pre-scene)
Purpose: Read six exchanges and Mira's narrator permissions to distinguish the spoken invitation from supplied private-character context.
Fixture: Character: Close narration may include Mira's fictional inner thoughts. She fears repeating last winter's argument with guest Eli. Chat: Eli arrives unexpectedly. Mira says, 'Of course you can stay.' The player controls Eli's response.
Inspect: Confirm the old argument is supplied and Mira's narration permits inner thoughts. The source does not reveal Eli's private feelings or establish a new argument.

Mira's relevant history (pre-state)
Purpose: Read actual actor-state Data to ground character history and avoid treating an invented inner line as memory.
Fixture: Select Mira as active actor. Existing supported history can qualify the old argument; empty scoped State is valid because the card supplies it. The example imports no live memory seed.
Inspect: Inspect scope, version and supplied history. Wire the same State and Scene to Reflect and Express; no fictional prose is committed by this Pre graph.

Hospitality with apprehension (pre-reflect)
Purpose: Create Reflection Data interpreting the difference between Mira's outward invitation and her supplied concern.
Inspect: Inspect brief/conflicts for grounded tension rather than a new backstory. Reflection is an assessment, not access to real private thoughts.

Output tokens includes visible text and any reasoning tokens counted by the provider. A truncated result is discarded; inspect the error, then manually raise the cap and rerun. No automatic retry occurs.

Mira's fictional unsaid line (pre-inner-voice)
Purpose: Use one Prose request to turn the assessment into brief authored characterization that adds information beyond the dialogue.
Inspect: Inspect Text marked fictional. The requested word range is advisory; maxTokens caps the request. This is character writing, never hidden model reasoning.

Output tokens includes visible text and any reasoning tokens counted by the provider. A truncated result is discarded; inspect the error, then manually raise the cap and rerun. No automatic retry occurs.

Label optional inner narration (pre-compose)
Purpose: Convert connected fictional Text into Guidance through the named InnerVoice section, with an explicit public/private boundary.
Inspect: Wire Express Text to section.InnerVoice. Inspect the labeled Guidance. The empty fallback is deliberate; a section accepts Text, never Guidance, and missing template paths fail.

Inner voice writing direction (pre-guidance)
Purpose: Expose the labeled optional character prose as a bounded Host result, leaving actual presentation to the native narrator.
Inspect: Check the label and narration boundary in the Host result. This workflow uses at most Analysis+Prose once each and neither applies a reply nor writes memory.

pre-reflect.title: Reflect · character
pre-reflect.instructions:
Appraise Mira saying 'Of course you can stay' after Eli's unexpected arrival, against the supplied old argument and current state. Keep the invitation as observation and apprehension about repetition as interpretation grounded in the card/history. Preserve hospitality and her wish for a limit without deciding a new dispute occurs. Provide a brief and conflicts suitable for a short fictional inner voice. Do not repeat the spoken line as the entire characterization, invent details of last winter, or assign the player's Eli any private thought or action.

Return one raw JSON object, beginning with { and ending with }. No Markdown, fences or preface. Use at most two items in each reflection array and one concise sentence for brief.

pre-inner-voice.title: Express · inner-voice
pre-inner-voice.instructions: Write 35–55 words of fictional close third-person inner voice for Mira. Use clipped practical thoughts: a spare cup, a spare chair, one night at a time. Let hospitality coexist with worry about the supplied old argument. Add subtext beyond 'Of course you can stay' without quoting her spoken line again. Do not invent how the old argument began, decide Eli's response, reveal his private state or claim model reasoning. Return only fictional prose; no explanation, heading or diagnostic text.
